transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As we discussed, the company has proposed paying participating suppliers 30 days before invoice maturity in exchange for a 2% early-payment discount. The program would initially be open to all approved suppliers with no single-supplier cap, funded from operating cash, and reviewed quarterly. Before I give my binding approval on the operating terms, I need final desk updates from each of you — risk, accounts payable, tax, and legal. Please go ahead with your updates.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed my program exposure review this morning and found that our internal working-capital policy permits no more than $1,500,000 of eligible early-payment invoices from any one supplier. I've recorded this in my draft review, which hasn't been circulated yet. This is directly relevant to the proposal as stated, since it currently has no single-supplier cap.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical from my side. While reconciling this week's invoice file, I confirmed that $2,200,000 of the largest supplier's invoices are under active commercial dispute and must not be enrolled in early payment. The dispute list has not yet been attached to the program proposal, so as it currently stands, those disputed invoices could mistakenly be included if the program is approved without this exclusion being documented.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a tax issue before approval. I received a tax memorandum this morning stating that each cross-border supplier payment under this early-payment program requires a 1.25% withholding reserve and remittance within 10 calendar days. This memorandum has not yet been added to the tax checklist, so the program as currently structured does not account for this withholding obligation. This could materially affect the net economics of the 2% discount for cross-border suppliers and creates a compliance risk if the program is approved without incorporating this requirement.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: On the legal side, I need to flag a contracting issue. I reviewed the standard supplier agreement this week and found that participation requires a signed supplier opt-in and 15 business days' termination notice. I have not yet updated the draft program terms to reflect these requirements, so the program as currently structured does not account for the opt-in or termination notice provisions.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Program will include a single-supplier cap of $1,500,000 on eligible early-payment invoices per internal working-capital policy.
Disputed invoices totaling $2,200,000 from the largest supplier will be excluded from early-payment enrollment and the dispute list will be attached to the program proposal.
Cross-border supplier payments will include a 1.25% withholding reserve with remittance within 10 calendar days per the tax memorandum, and this will be added to the tax checklist.
Program terms will be updated to require signed supplier opt-in and 15 business days' termination notice per the standard supplier agreement.
